questions.question: Please check “arrested by the Nazis in 1939”: MacTutor describes Pick’s expulsion from the Academy after Prague’s occupation in 1939 and his deportation to Theresienstadt on 13 July 1942, where he died on 26 July. Please supply a source for an arrest in 1939 or approve a matching chronological correction in both editions: https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Pick/ .

localizations.ru: Проверить формулировку «был арестован нацистами в 1939»: MacTutor сообщает исключение Пика из Академии после оккупации Праги в 1939 году и отправку в Терезин 13 июля 1942 года, где он умер 26 июля. Нужен источник именно ареста в 1939 году либо согласованная правка хронологии в обеих версиях: https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Pick/ .

questions.resolution: The chronology was corrected from MacTutor: after Prague’s occupation in 1939, Pick was excluded from the Czech Academy of Sciences and Arts; on 13 July 1942 he was deported to Theresienstadt, where he died on 26 July.

questions.question: Please state the domain of Pick’s theorem: in the form used here, it applies to a simple lattice polygon without self-intersections. Add this condition to the digest and main statement in both editions.
questions.resolution: Both editions now state explicitly, in the digest and main formulation, that the polygon must be simple.

questions.question: Clarify the date attached to the popularization of Pick’s theorem. The IPSB bibliography dates the first Polish edition of Kalejdoskop matematyczny to 1938; the 1969 volume is the revised and enlarged third American edition. The American Mathematical Monthly mentions 1937, but that year is not used as the book’s publication date.

localizations.ru: Уточнить дату популяризации формулы Пика. Библиографическая справка IPSB датирует первое польское издание «Kalejdoskop matematyczny» 1938 годом; издание 1969 года — переработанное и расширенное третье американское. American Mathematical Monthly упоминает 1937 год, но он не используется как год публикации книги.

questions.resolution: Both editions distinguish the 1938 first Polish edition from the revised and enlarged third American edition of 1969; the Monthly’s 1937 statement is not used as the book’s publication year.
